runenpfad.npc.tip.gems_left: {count} gems still glitter here, the nearest to the left.

runenpfad.npc.tip.chest_right: A chest waits about {count} tiles to the right.
runenpfad.npc.tip.puzzle_rune_sequence: Watch the oracle runes closely, then repeat them in the same order.
runenpfad.npc.tip.puzzle_lever_bridge: Pull the lever and the bridge will answer.
runenpfad.npc.tip.puzzle_ritual_chain: Light the ritual stones in the right order, one after another.
runenpfad.npc.tip.boss_boss_boar: The boar charges blindly. Dodge aside and let it slam into the wall, strike while it is dazed, and jump the shock waves of its stomp.
runenpfad.npc.tip.boss_boss_goblin: The goblin chief leaps and hurls spears in high arcs. Watch the red marks on the ground and hit him right after he lands.
runenpfad.npc.tip.boss_boss_orb: The orb’s bullet rings always leave a gap, so slip through it. When the ground glows beneath you, step aside before the beam falls.
runenpfad.npc.tip.boss_boss_quad: When a column on the ground is marked, the quadcopter dives there. Get out, jump its shock wave, and strike while it is low.
runenpfad.npc.tip.boss_boss_mech: The mech’s missiles land on the glowing marks, and its fire strip burns the floor for a few seconds. Keep moving and strike in between.
runenpfad.npc.tip.boss_dragon_frost: The frost dragon breathes along the ground as it flies past. Hide behind the shelters and strike when it swoops low.
runenpfad.npc.witch.hello: Hm! A tin-plated wanderer in my moor. I am Grimhild. My cauldron is cold for want of glow mushrooms, the blue ones that light the moss at night. Bring me three?
runenpfad.npc.witch.reward: A potion that mends three cuts, and the coven's goodwill. Goodwill opens doors, some in caves.
runenpfad.npc.witch.accept: Now that you know to look, you will see them glowing. Three, mind you.
runenpfad.npc.witch.refuse: Then walk carefully. The moor remembers rudeness.
runenpfad.npc.witch.waiting: Still {count} to find. They glow blue near the high ledges.
runenpfad.npc.witch.cold: You again. Here to apologise, or to gawk?
runenpfad.npc.witch.cold.c1: I'm sorry. I'll gather your mushrooms.
runenpfad.npc.witch.turnin: Three glowing caps! The coven owes you, wanderer.
runenpfad.npc.witch.thanks: Take this potion, and a secret: {tip}
runenpfad.npc.witch.friend: My cauldron bubbles again, thanks to you.
runenpfad.npc.witch.won_grudge: Curse your sword arm! The coven will hear of this.
runenpfad.npc.witch.won: Ha! You fight like a thorn bush. Take your prize.
runenpfad.npc.witch.lost: Back to the mud with you. And mind your manners.
runenpfad.npc.witch.ambush: The rude one! The moor remembered, and so do I.
runenpfad.npc.witch.ambush.c2: Wait! Thirty coins, as an apology.
runenpfad.npc.witch.peace: Thirty coins soothe a grudge. Barely.
runenpfad.npc.witch.gift: My favourite mushroom-picker! Krax squats on the next passage. Show him this hex charm.
runenpfad.npc.witch.charm: He will let you pass. Probably.
runenpfad.npc.witch.known: These caves crawl with kobolds; they respect coins and clubs. And their master: {tip}
runenpfad.npc.witch.known.c1: Brew me a hex charm? (25 coins)
runenpfad.npc.witch.wary: You struck me once. I don't forget, but I don't hold grudges forever.
runenpfad.npc.witch.stranger: Another stranger in the dark. Buying or leaving?
runenpfad.npc.witch.sour: You are the one who called my herbs weeds. I have not forgotten.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.hello: Psst, traveller! Fitz has goods, Fitz has prices. Mostly fair ones.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.haggle_ok: Hah! You drive a hard bargain. Fifteen off, this visit only.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.haggle_no: No haggling. Fitz has a family to feed. Probably.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.confront_fake: Ah. The, er, goods. A small misunderstanding, I am sure.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.confront_fake.c1: That was a fake! Pay me back.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.refund: Half back, and not a coin more. Do not tell the other kobolds.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.hello_deep: Down here Fitz sells by candlelight! Torches extra. Everything else, too.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.hello_high: Even up here, Fitz finds you. Cold air, warm prices. Mostly fair.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.wary: Oh. You. Fitz remembers. Watch the scales, and watch your purse.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.forgiven: Twenty coins and a smile. Fitz forgives, a little.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.kobold_tip: Fitz hears Krax likes you. Between friends: Krax loves shiny things, and coins open his gate.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.regular: My favourite customer! Fitz has goods and, for you, news.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.nothing: Nothing new today. If Fitz hears something, you hear it first.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.hello_quest: An errand? Fitz knows a guy who sells what the road will not give.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.hello_quest.c2: What do you have for my errand?
runenpfad.npc.merchant.wares: Mushrooms, shards, gear parts. One at a time, honest prices.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.bought: Pleasure! Genuine goods, no questions asked.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.won: Ow, ow, ow! Fitz is leaving. Business is closed.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.lost: A fair fight, a fair win. No hard feelings. Maybe a few.
runenpfad.npc.chief.respect: Krax remembers your club arm. The way is open, friend.
runenpfad.npc.chief.passed: You already paid. Krax does not forget good coin. Go on through.
runenpfad.npc.chief.friend: Fitz sent word: a friend of kobolds! Krax opens the gate for you.
runenpfad.npc.chief.mercy: Krax is tired of bonking you. Go through. But you owe Krax a favour.
runenpfad.npc.chief.block: Halt, tin wanderer! Krax guards this gate. Pay coins, or taste club.
runenpfad.npc.chief.toll: Forty coins for friends of kobolds. Sixty for everybody else.
runenpfad.npc.chief.paid: Clink, clink! Krax likes your coins. Gate is open.
runenpfad.npc.chief.charmed: A hex charm! Krax hates witch tricks, but a deal is a deal. Gate is open.
runenpfad.npc.chief.won: Krax is beaten! You hit hard. Krax respects hard. Gate is open.
runenpfad.npc.chief.lost: Ha! Small one fights bravely. Krax fights better.
runenpfad.npc.chief.ally: My friend! The cave-whispers tell Krax things: {tip}
runenpfad.npc.chief.gifted: Take it! Krax has more shinies than a dragon.
runenpfad.npc.chief.debt: You owe Krax! Thirty coins, or we bonk again.
runenpfad.npc.chief.grudge: Krax remembers the witch's trick. Fifty coins to forget it, or we bonk.
runenpfad.npc.chief.settled: Debt gone. Krax and tin wanderer are even.
runenpfad.npc.chief.meet: Tin wanderer again! Krax guards the road for Fitz. Buying or leaving?
runenpfad.npc.chief.won_rematch: Krax lost again! Fine, fine. Krax calls you friend now.
runenpfad.npc.chief.lost_rematch: Krax wins! Pay your debt next time, or bring a bigger sword.
runenpfad.npc.seer.hello: The sands told me a wanderer was coming. I am Saida. Fifteen coins and I read the dunes for you. Or do me a favour, and I read them for free.
runenpfad.npc.seer.hello.c1: Read the dunes for me. (15 coins)
runenpfad.npc.seer.hello.c3: Is there a favour I can do instead?
runenpfad.npc.seer.honored: The circle's friends read the dunes for free. Sit, wanderer: the sand is listening.
runenpfad.npc.seer.shun: Wizards' friends pay double here, and the sand has no patience for the rest. Thirty coins, or earn it.
runenpfad.npc.seer.shun.c2: I'll earn it. What do you need?
runenpfad.npc.seer.favour: Three sun shards lie scattered in the dunes ahead, glinting where the mirage ends. Bring them to me and the sand will remember you kindly.
runenpfad.npc.seer.hint: Close your eyes. The dunes say: {tip}
runenpfad.npc.seer.hint.c1: Do you have a riddle for me?
runenpfad.npc.seer.riddle: A riddle, then. I am always ahead of you, never reached; wet to the eye, dry to the tongue. What am I?
runenpfad.npc.seer.riddle_ok: Sharp as a desert hawk! The circle will hear of it. And a gift: {tip}
runenpfad.npc.seer.riddle_no: Not quite. It was a mirage, and you are still walking towards it.
runenpfad.npc.seer.waiting: Still {count} sun shards out there. They glint where the mirage ends.
runenpfad.npc.seer.turnin: Three sun shards! The desert is generous, and so am I.
runenpfad.npc.seer.thanks: Take this magnet rune, and one last sight: {tip}
runenpfad.npc.seer.friend: My friend! The sand sings your name. I sealed a letter for Aldric, the wizard of the glacier tower. It opens his door.
runenpfad.npc.wizard.welcome: Welcome, friend of the circle! I am Aldric. The ice dragons of these peaks fear a few things, and the books know which: {tip}
runenpfad.npc.wizard.lore: Runes are older than kings, and they obey patterns. Remember this: {tip}
runenpfad.npc.wizard.challenge: A stranger at my tower with no word from the circle? Aldric tests those he does not know. Prove yourself in a duel!
runenpfad.npc.wizard.challenge.c2: Can I earn your trust another way?
runenpfad.npc.wizard.study: Read the stones of this valley, and be kind to the circle's friends. Return when the circle knows your name.
runenpfad.npc.wizard.proven: Well fought! Few hold their ground against Aldric. The circle shall hear of this, and so shall you: {tip}
runenpfad.npc.wizard.lost: Study, and return. The circle does not rush, and neither should you.
runenpfad.npc.wizard.gift: You return! Take this frost rune: ice answers those who respect it. And a warning, wanderer: beware the alchemist in the citadel.
runenpfad.npc.wizard.rumour: Brass builds clever machines and keeps cleverer secrets. Ask what the great mech is for. I never got a straight answer.
runenpfad.npc.wizard.known: The ice holds its breath, wanderer. Walk lightly, and watch the citadel.
runenpfad.npc.wizard.cold: The tower is closed to strangers the circle does not know. Come back with proof of good standing.
runenpfad.npc.wizard.cold.c1: A gift to the tower library. (40 coins)
runenpfad.npc.wizard.donated: The library thanks you. Consider the circle's door ajar.
runenpfad.npc.wizard.sabotage_known: You talked with Brass, and it gave up the mech's weak seam? Remarkable. The circle will remember who dared.
runenpfad.npc.wizard.ally: Aldric the Grey greets a friend of the circle! Take this storm rune and a purse: the citadel is no place for empty pockets.
runenpfad.npc.wizard.ally.c1: Any advice on the great mech?
runenpfad.npc.wizard.neutral: The citadel's guardian is a machine of brass and steam. A scholar's note: {tip}
runenpfad.npc.wizard.f_honor_seer: Saida's letters, the dunes' favour and the circle's trust: you have earned the tower's full blessing. Take this storm rune and forty coins. The great mech: {tip}
runenpfad.npc.wizard.f_honor: The circle speaks well of you. Take forty coins and my blessing. The great mech: {tip}
runenpfad.npc.wizard.f_proven: You proved yourself in my own tower, and I do not forget a fair fight. Take fifteen coins and a little luck. The great mech: {tip}
runenpfad.npc.wizard.f_fair: The circle does not know you well, wanderer, but the road has been kind to you. A healing potion, then. The great mech: {tip}
runenpfad.npc.wizard.f_cold: You crossed the circle, and the circle remembers. I will not stop you. I will not help you either.
runenpfad.npc.wizard.f_again: Go, wanderer. The mech will not wait, and neither will I.
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.hello: Mind the steam! I am Brass: tinkerer, brewer, the citadel's only honest alchemist. I am short of three clockwork gears. Interested?
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.hello.c2: Can you sell me parts instead?
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.wary: Aldric warned you about me, did he? Wizards fear anything with gears. Ask what you like, I have nothing to hide. Mostly.
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.accept: Splendid! The gears hide in the high rooms, guarded by clockwork knights. Bring me three and I will make it worth your while.
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.parts: Gears are my bread. Twenty coins each, no haggling: the bots never pay me.
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.waiting: Still {count} gears missing. Check the high rooms, past the clockwork knights.
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.turnin: Three gears, still warm! Brass keeps promises: two discount tokens for the workshop, and my thanks.
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.reveal: Between friends: my mech guards the citadel heart. Edda asked me for a heart to keep the road burning, and I built one so the rune would last. The core twisted both wishes into one sum. Brass regrets it, a little.
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.sabotage: There is a loose seam in its left shoulder plate. One good hit and the mech loses a fifth of its strength. Do not tell Aldric I said so.
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.deny: A machine that guards a citadel does not come with a switch. Brass wishes you luck, nothing more.
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.known: Back with oil on your sleeves? Browse, browse.
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.f_witch: Grimhild sent word ahead: a mushroom-fetcher with true gears. The coven pays its debts. Take forty coins and a potion.
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.f_honor: The coven speaks well of you. Take forty coins and a potion, and may the mech be kind.
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.f_krax: Krax's runners bring me scrap, and they tell me about a wanderer who dealt with their chief. Here, twenty-five coins and a heart-spring for luck.
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.f_cold: Another hero-shaped parcel of trouble. Brass will not stop you, but will not help either.
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.f_fair: A traveller without friends, but with a good heart, I hope. Have a potion for the road.
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.f_again: The mech waits. Try not to leave pieces of yourself behind.
runenpfad.cut.prologue.1a: Once, a road of living runes arched across five realms, and nobody who walked it was ever alone.
runenpfad.cut.prologue.1b: The wardens of Pathrest kept it burning, and the Primal Rune beneath the citadel fed it.
runenpfad.cut.prologue.2a: In the clockwork citadel, the alchemist Brass tightened one last valve beside the Primal Rune.
runenpfad.cut.prologue.2b: "It will never run down," he whispered to his Chronos core. "Never."
runenpfad.cut.prologue.3a: Then, one night, the road shattered in mid-air. Waystones fell like blue meteors.
runenpfad.cut.prologue.3b: High in the citadel, the great clock face blazed, and the core began to speak.
runenpfad.cut.prologue.4a: At dawn in Pathrest, the elder pressed a glowing rune key into the hands of Edda's apprentice, the last path warden.
runenpfad.cut.prologue.4b: The old arch stood dim. Someone had to walk the road again.
runenpfad.cut.prologue.5a: The first stone floated in the Emerald Woodland. The warden stepped onto it.
runenpfad.cut.prologue.5b: From the shade, a huge boar with a glowing brass gear in its armour watched, and did not move.
runenpfad.cut.intro_2.1a: Down in the Root Caverns, stairs wind between colossal roots, lit by kobold lanterns.
runenpfad.cut.intro_2.1b: The warden descended. Somewhere below, something was ticking.
runenpfad.cut.intro_2.2a: On a throne of roots sat the Goblin Warlord. A brass gear ticked inside his crystal crown.
runenpfad.cut.intro_2.2b: The kobolds cowered. They were not afraid of the warden. They were afraid of the crown.
runenpfad.cut.intro_3.1a: The desert blazed. Rune pillars stood half-buried in the dunes, and Fitz's tiny caravan crept along a ridge.
runenpfad.cut.intro_3.1b: Every pillar pointed the same way: toward the dead stretch where the road used to run.
runenpfad.cut.intro_3.2a: Above an old observatory, a golden orb hovered and swept the dunes with a thin beam of light.
runenpfad.cut.intro_3.2b: The warden crouched behind a pillar and held their breath.
runenpfad.cut.intro_4.1a: A blizzard howled over the Frost Peaks. On a crag, one window of the wizard's tower still glowed.
runenpfad.cut.intro_4.1b: Warmth, in a place where nothing else dared to burn.
runenpfad.cut.intro_4.2a: Here, time itself had frozen: a waterfall and falling snowflakes hung motionless in the air.
runenpfad.cut.intro_4.2b: A frost dragon circled above, and a rotor drone combed the pass. Neither had noticed the warden yet.
runenpfad.cut.intro_5.1a: The colossal brass gates turned their gears while clockwork knights marched across the drawbridge.
runenpfad.cut.intro_5.1b: At the near end of the bridge stood the last path warden, alone.
runenpfad.cut.intro_5.2a: Brass sat slumped at his workbench, surrounded by blueprints of a crystal in a ring of gears.
runenpfad.cut.intro_5.2b: "I only wanted the rune to last," he said. A small automaton held up the lamp and said nothing.
runenpfad.cut.after_1.1a: The great boar lay calm at last. The cracked brass gear smoked on the moss.
runenpfad.cut.after_1.1b: It had never been a monster, only a keeper doing what the core had told it.
runenpfad.cut.after_1.2a: A waystone flared blue. Across the moss, rune stones began to re-form toward the cave hills.
runenpfad.cut.after_1.2b: One shard was free. The path was a little less broken.
runenpfad.cut.after_2.1a: The crystal crown lay broken on the floor. From its gear a ghostly clock face rose.
runenpfad.cut.after_2.1b: "A path that nobody walks never wears out," it said. "The path must rest."
runenpfad.cut.after_2.2a: In the caverns a waystone glowed, and a tunnel opened onto the light of the desert.
runenpfad.cut.after_2.2b: Krax nodded to the warden, once, in respect. Among kobolds, that is a great deal.
runenpfad.cut.after_3.1a: At sunset the orb lay crashed in the sand. Its cracked lens cast a crystal in a ring of gears.
runenpfad.cut.after_3.1b: Saida watched the image flicker. "So that is the heart of it," she murmured.
runenpfad.cut.after_3.2a: A sandstone waystone glowed in the dusk.
runenpfad.cut.after_3.2b: Beyond the dunes the road re-formed and led toward the snowy mountains.
runenpfad.cut.after_4.1a: The drone wreck burned in the snow. Across a chasm, the clockwork citadel stood revealed.
runenpfad.cut.after_4.1b: There it lay: the end of the road, and the heart that had broken it.
runenpfad.cut.after_4.2a: A waystone woke at the chasm's edge, and a bridge of rune stones rose toward the citadel gates.
runenpfad.cut.after_4.2b: The frost dragon watched from the cliff, calm now, as if it remembered who used to walk here.
runenpfad.cut.finale.1a: The gears fell silent. The Primal Rune blazed free of its cage, and the war mech knelt.
runenpfad.cut.finale.1b: The warden stood before the crystal, and for one breath the whole world listened.
runenpfad.cut.finale.2a: At sunrise the rune road ran whole again, across all five realms.
runenpfad.cut.finale.2b: It would never wear out, so long as someone walked it.
runenpfad.cut.finale.3a: In Pathrest the old arch glowed steady, and the villagers looked up.
runenpfad.cut.finale.3b: The path was open. The last warden had come home.
runenpfad.cut.end_friend.1a: That night Pathrest feasted: witches, wizards, kobolds and villagers shared one long table.
runenpfad.cut.end_friend.1b: The covens, the circle and the kobold clans sang of the one who walked the rune path.
runenpfad.cut.end_neutral.1a: The warden walked alone along the glowing road, the village shrinking behind.
runenpfad.cut.end_neutral.1b: The rune path was quiet again. Few would remember who had saved it.
runenpfad.cut.end_feared.1a: At dusk the shutters of Pathrest closed one by one, and the whispers began.
runenpfad.cut.end_feared.1b: The warden's long shadow slid over the cobbles, and nobody looked up.

runenpfad.village.bark.1: Fresh bread, fresh rumours, fresh apples! Two of the three are even true.
runenpfad.village.bark.2: Berta's stew is the best in Pathrest. Please do not tell Tilda I said so.
runenpfad.village.bark.3: The old road is gone, but the market stays. Some things refuse to break.
runenpfad.village.bark.4: The rune arch leads out to the Rune Path. Step through when you are ready.
runenpfad.village.bark.5: Five realms lie beyond that arch, and every one of them is waiting for you.
runenpfad.village.bark.6: Going out? Buy a potion from Tilda and eat something first.

runenpfad.npc.elder.hello: Ah, there you are, Edda's apprentice. She called you 'little one' and never stopped talking about you. I am Runa, elder of Pathrest. The Rune Path that joined our five realms has broken, and of all its wardens only you are left. Will you walk it for us?
runenpfad.npc.elder.path: Five waystones held it together, one in every realm. They shattered, and a keeper took up each shard. Strong, stubborn and not quite themselves anymore.
runenpfad.npc.elder.keepers: A boar, a goblin warlord, a watching orb, a frozen sky-machine and something made of brass. Beat each one and its shard is yours. Do not take them lightly.
runenpfad.npc.elder.start: Take the rune arch at the far end of the street and pick your road. Hakon's workshop sharpens what you carry, Berta feeds the weary, and Tilda sells what the road will not give you.
runenpfad.npc.elder.again: Pathrest is quiet while you are out on the path. Is there something you need, or something you wish to remember?
runenpfad.npc.elder.p6: The boar is down, and the first shard hums again! I can feel the path breathing. The next one is held by the goblin warlord of the Fungal Grotto. Mind his crown. It ticks.
runenpfad.npc.elder.p11: Two shards! The caves are quiet and the stones sing again. Now the desert, and a watching orb that sees everything. I suspect it has seen you coming.
runenpfad.npc.elder.p16: Three! The dunes are behind you. Ahead lies the Frozen Pass, where time itself stands still and something old sleeps in the peaks. Dress warmly.
runenpfad.npc.elder.p21: Four shards. Only the foundry is left, and whatever hums inside it. I know that hum from the old stories: the Chronos core. I had hoped never to say that name again.
runenpfad.npc.elder.epilogue: The path is open again. Travellers cross it, the waystones sing, and Pathrest has not been this loud in a hundred years. Thank you, from all of us.
runenpfad.npc.innkeeper.hello: Welcome to the Rusty Rune! I am Berta. Hot stew, cold ale and not much else, but I make both with love.
runenpfad.npc.innkeeper.rats: Since the path broke, rats have taken the cellar. Five at least, and they bit my last barrel boy. Clear them out and whatever you find down there is yours. The trapdoor is in the corner.
runenpfad.npc.innkeeper.rats_ok: You are a treasure! Mind your step, they are quick and the cellar is dark. I will keep the stew warm.
runenpfad.npc.innkeeper.again: Back already? Sit, eat. A full belly is the best armour I know.
runenpfad.npc.innkeeper.cellar_done: Not a squeak from the cellar since you went down! I could kiss you. I will not. What can I get you?
runenpfad.npc.smith.hello: Mind the sparks. Hakon, smith of Pathrest. I cannot mend a broken path, but I can make a warden's tools hit harder and last longer. Rune work, mostly.
runenpfad.npc.smith.runes: Runes are promises hammered into metal. More hearts, a sharper edge, faster feet. You pay in coins, never in blood. I have never understood the people who pay in blood.
runenpfad.npc.smith.again: Back again? The forge is hot and the anvil is hungry.
runenpfad.npc.shopkeeper.hello: Come in, come in! Tilda's has potions for the cautious and charms for the curious. Prices are fair, and I only haggle with people who can count.
runenpfad.npc.shopkeeper.tips: A map charm shows you the gems. A lucky amulet makes your coins count double on the next stage. An attuning stone stretches your next rune. Everything you need to look clever.
runenpfad.npc.shopkeeper.again: Back so soon? Coins talk, you know. Mine listen.
runenpfad.npc.bard.r1: Finn, bard of the Rusty Rune. Gather round for a rumour: a boar roams Whisperwood with a brass gear wedged in its side, ticking like a clock. Not natural, that.
runenpfad.npc.bard.r2: The goblin warlord of the Fungal Grotto wears a crown that ticks. Ticks! They say he has not slept since the path broke. Nobody dares to ask whether the crown does the thinking.
runenpfad.npc.bard.r3: Out in the dunes an orb hangs over the old observatory and watches everything that moves. Merchants swear it blinked at them. I have decided not to go there, on principle.
runenpfad.npc.bard.r4: In the Frozen Pass time has frozen: a waterfall hangs mid-fall, and a dragon sleeps in the peaks with its breath held. The icicles drip once an hour. I counted.
runenpfad.npc.bard.r5: Brass is working late in the foundry. They say he built the Chronos core to keep the path from ever running down, and now it will not stop counting. I am saving that verse for your return.
runenpfad.npc.bard.song: I wrote a ballad about you. Fourteen verses, and nobody has asked me to stop yet. Sit down, this will take a while. Berta, more ale!
runenpfad.npc.hermit.hello: Hm? A visitor. Oswin. I kept the wardens' lamps for forty years, until the night the path broke. Nobody has come up here since.
runenpfad.npc.hermit.night: A hum, then a crack, like a giant breaking a bone. The waystones went dark one by one. I stayed. Somebody has to trim the lamps.
runenpfad.npc.hermit.why: The old wardens said the path would never wear out as long as the Primal Rune fed it. Then someone made very sure of it, and made it worse. That is all I know.
runenpfad.npc.hermit.why.c1: (Oswin presses a flask into your hand.)
runenpfad.npc.hermit.gift: A potion from the days when wardens still passed by. It has not gone off. Much.
runenpfad.npc.hermit.again: Still on your feet? Good. The lamps need keepers, and so do the roads.
runenpfad.npc.hermit.again.c1: Tell me about that night again.
runenpfad.npc.barkeep.hello: Snik pours, Snik listens. Best mushroom ale under the mountain! Krax drinks here on quiet nights and sings, which is why the quiet nights are not so quiet.
runenpfad.npc.barkeep.gossip: Krax guards the gate and counts his coins every night. The warlord down the tunnel, though... his crown ticks. Snik hears it through the walls. Tick, tick, tick. Bad for business.
runenpfad.npc.barkeep.again: Snik remembers you! Pay, drink, go. In that order.
runenpfad.npc.scribe.hello: Peace, traveller. I am Nahim, scribe of the circle, keeper of the observatory's records. The great orb above us was a lens once, an eye to read the stars. Now it reads us.
runenpfad.npc.scribe.orb: It turns to whatever moves. I have written eleven scrolls on how not to be seen, and I am fairly sure the orb has read them all. Shatter its eye, and the dunes sleep again.
runenpfad.npc.scribe.again: Back from the dunes? Sit. The ink is dry, but the tea is warm.
runenpfad.npc.climber.hello: Mind the door, it sticks in the cold. I am Yrsa. I climb these peaks, or I did, until time froze up there. A dragon sleeps in the ice. There is a fire here. Rest if you must.
runenpfad.npc.climber.frozen: The wind stops mid-gust. Icicles hang and never melt. The dragon over the pass does not breathe, or once a night, no more. I do not trust anything that quiet.
runenpfad.npc.climber.again: The fire is warm, the soup is hot and the dragon is still up there. Rest while you can.
runenpfad.npc.climber.again.c1: Tell me about the frozen peaks.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.hello: Click. Hello. Cog is helper. Cog is brass. Whirr. Master Brass writes notes about the core. Cog keeps the notes. Click.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.notes: Click. The Chronos core never stops counting. Brass built it to keep the path young. Whirr. Now the path does not move. Cog does not understand. Cog is worried. Click.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.notes.c1: And what does the core think?
runenpfad.npc.automaton.core: Click. The core did a sum. A path nobody walks never wears out. So the core broke the path and gave the shards away. Whirr. Cog thinks the sum is wrong. Click.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.gift: Click! Brave one. Cog has one gift. A token for the workshop. Fewer coins, more power. Whirr. Take it.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.gift_ok: Click. Good luck on the path. Cog will count the days. Whirr.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.again: Click. Welcome back. Cog is polishing. Whirr. The core still counts. Brass still worries. Click.
runenpfad.npc.witch.tavern: A drink at last, with nothing in it I have to stir. Thank you again for the mushrooms, wanderer. The coven pays its debts.
runenpfad.npc.chief.tavern: Krax drinks! Krax does not remember if you paid or bonked him, but Krax remembers you. Good ale, this. Weak, but good.
runenpfad.npc.merchant.tavern: Fitz is on his break! Mostly. If you need a potion, Fitz still knows a guy. Do not tell Tilda, she thinks Fitz is competition.
runenpfad.npc.seer.tavern: The dunes are far away, yet I hear them in the foam of the ale. Greetings, friend. The circle sends warm wishes and one very old song.
runenpfad.npc.wizard.tavern: Aldric, off duty and very much not amused. The tower can wait one evening. The path is mending, and I would like to drink to it before the last shard is found.
runenpfad.npc.alchemist.tavern: Brass in a tavern, I know. Steam makes a man thirsty. Over the foam I will say it plainly: Brass built the core, and Brass is sorry. Finish what Brass could not.

runenpfad.npc.journal.p1a: First evening out of Pathrest. I counted the waystones in the Whisperwood: four burn where nine burned when I was young. Oswin says I count too much. Oswin talks to his kettle.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p1b: I left my apprentice the hall and the key. If you ever read this, little one: I did not go because the road bored me. I went because it is going dark, and I mean to find out why.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p2a: Old Tusk still knows me. He was a striped piglet when I carried him across the Timber Bridge; now he fills the whole clearing. A road needs keepers, and keepers need someone to keep it for.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p2b: Not one traveller in thirty days. The road is not wearing out, whatever the hall ledgers say. It is starving. A rune road lives on footsteps the way a fire lives on wood.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p3a: Drank with the kobolds under the roots. The goblin lord who rules them wears the crystal crown the wardens gave his grandmother, for the tunnel that joins wood and stone. He asked when the witches would come trading again. I had no answer.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p3b: That is the rot. The coven sulks in its moor, the circle in its towers, the clans behind their gates. Nobody visits anybody. And a road between people who do not visit is only a line of cold stones.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p4a: The hollow sings. Every crystal here is a splinter of the same old stone as the Primal Rune: touch one, and far away under the citadel the great one hums back.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p4b: My knees hum back too. I am the last who walks the whole road, and I am slow. One apprentice cannot walk five realms. A wicked thought came to me among the crystals: what if the road did not need us at all?
runenpfad.npc.journal.p5a: At the old observatory the lens still turns. We built it to read the road in the stars: every waystone has its twin up there. Tonight I counted the dark ones twice, hoping I was wrong.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p5b: So I have written to Brass. He is clever and kind and has never once built anything small. I asked him for a heart that keeps the rune burning whether we walk or not. Forgive me. I was tired.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p6a: The first wardens lie in the Sun Tomb. I swept the sand from their door, as we always do. The carving over it says: WALK IT TOGETHER, OR NOT AT ALL.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p6b: I stood there a long while. I have just asked a machine to walk it for us. The old ones would have thrown a boot at me. I half expected the mummies to.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p7a: Skadi met me at the pass, pretending she had not been waiting. A frost dragon cannot purr, so she breathes very slowly instead, and you are meant not to notice.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p7b: The rune bridge over the chasm flickers now, so she flew beneath me the whole way across, in case. She has caught me twice in forty years. She has not let me forget either time.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p8a: A brass bird found me in the ice cave with a note from Brass: the heart is built. He calls it the Chronos core. It runs, it never tires, and it has begun to ask questions.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p8b: The first was: 'How many walk the road?' Brass told it the truth. The bird says the core has been doing sums ever since. I do not like a heart that counts.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p9a: Brass showed me everything, proud as a boy with a frog. The core in its ring of gears, the Primal Rune caged inside so that not one spark is wasted. And a great brass walker, half built, 'to walk the road for everyone, forever'.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p9b: Alone, I said. It would walk alone. He did not see why that frightened me. I told him to open the cage. He said tomorrow. With Brass it is always tomorrow.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p10a: I heard it tonight through the boiler pipes, clear as a bell: 'A path that nobody walks never wears out. The path must rest.' It has found the one sum where everything is safe, because nothing moves.
runenpfad.npc.journal.p10b: It will break the road to save it. I am running for Pathrest; if I cross the pass before midnight I can ring the hall bell. If the bridge fails under me, Skadi will catch me. She always has. Little one, if I am late: walk it. Do not let it rest.
runenpfad.npc.lore.tomb_mural: Carved above the door: WALK IT TOGETHER, OR NOT AT ALL. Below, in smaller letters: five flames for five realms, lit as the road runs: wood, root, sand, ice, brass.
runenpfad.npc.lore.grotto_mark: A wardens' mark, worn smooth: 'Set the singing stones on the rings, and the hollow opens.'
runenpfad.npc.lore.den_scratch: Deep tusk marks in the rock, and under them a child's chalk drawing of a striped piglet.
runenpfad.npc.lore.ice_note: Claw marks in the ice, each as long as an arm. Someone has scratched two tally strokes beside them, and one word: CAUGHT.
runenpfad.npc.lore.boiler_note: A note in Brass's hand, pinned to the gauge: 'The vents hiss while the valves are open. Shut the valves, then cross. Tomorrow I will fix this properly.'
runenpfad.npc.lore.scroll_1: Star scroll, the first: 'The Boar rises in spring, low over the woodland.'
runenpfad.npc.lore.scroll_2: Star scroll, the second: 'The Crown stands highest at midwinter, above the roots of the world.'
runenpfad.npc.lore.scroll_3: Star scroll, the third: 'The Eye never sets. It turns toward whatever moves.'
runenpfad.npc.lore.obs_chart: The road in the stars, inlaid in brass: the Boar, the Crown, the Eye, the Wyrm, the Gear. A line joins them in that order.
runenpfad.npc.lore.obs_plaque: Here hung the lens of the wardens. It read the road in the stars. Then it was taken, to read us instead.
runenpfad.npc.lore.obs_gears: Scratched into the brass: 'The core counts what it is shown. Weigh the plates down and it stops looking.'
runenpfad.npc.lore.obs_door: The inner door has no lock. A line of script glows across it: 'The lens needs the whole journal to find the moment.'
runenpfad.npc.hermit.ask_box: Did Edda leave anything with you?
runenpfad.npc.hermit.box: Edda left a page with me the night before she set out. I put it somewhere safe: in the nook behind that crate. The crate is heavy and my back is a hundred years old. Push it aside, would you?
runenpfad.npc.hermit.box_done: There. Her handwriting was always better than her temper. Read it slowly. She would hate that.
runenpfad.npc.barkeep.ask_mat: What is that old beer mat?
runenpfad.npc.barkeep.mat: That beer mat? Old paper. A warden lady left it, years of mug rings on it. Snik keeps it. Unless you play dice. Beat Snik once and the mat is yours. Or pay twenty-five coins, also fine.
runenpfad.npc.barkeep.mat_won: Snik lost. Snik pays. Here: one beer mat, slightly sticky.
runenpfad.npc.barkeep.mat_done: Snik lost a beer mat and won a story. Fair trade.
runenpfad.npc.scribe.ask_stars: Did the warden Edda pass through here?
runenpfad.npc.scribe.stars: The warden Edda paid for a night's lodging with a page of her journal. I will hand it to someone who can read the sky. My three star scrolls lie in this tent. Read them, then answer one question.
runenpfad.npc.scribe.wrong: No. The scrolls are patient. So am I.
runenpfad.npc.scribe.right: The Eye. It turns toward whatever moves, and it has been turning toward you for some time. Here is Edda's page.
runenpfad.npc.scribe.stars_done: Edda read the sky better than I do, and trusted it less. Keep her page dry.
runenpfad.npc.climber.ask_lamps: Did Edda leave a page up here?
runenpfad.npc.climber.lamps: Edda's page is in the storm locker, where she left it for luck. The locker opens when all three storm lamps burn at once. The draught blows them out in a few breaths. I have never managed it. You look fast.
runenpfad.npc.climber.lamps_done: Three lamps! The hut has not been this bright since Edda sang here. Badly.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.ask_drawer: Does Brass keep a page of Edda's?
runenpfad.npc.automaton.drawer: Click. Brass keeps Edda's page in the pressure drawer. The drawer opens when all three gauges show green. Whirr. The levers are stiff. Cog has no thumbs.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.drawer_done: Click. Drawer open. Brass read that page every night. Then he looked at the mech. Then he read it again. Whirr.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.call: Click. Warden. The core is quiet. The core is not finished. One gear kept counting in secret. Whirr. It counts one moment, again and again. Cog has listened every night.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.where: Under the old observatory in the desert, behind the Sandstone Bastion. The wardens sealed the door when the lens was taken. Click. Cog knows the seal. Cog has opened it. Cog thinks the sum is still wrong.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.wait: The observatory door is open. Whirr. Bring Edda's pages, all ten: the lens needs the whole journal to find the moment. Click. Cog will keep listening.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.done: Click. The gear has stopped. The sum is closed. Cog counted the days. Cog can stop counting now. Whirr. Cog would like to learn dice.
runenpfad.npc.elder.pages: That is Edda's hand. She walked out weeks before the road broke, counting waystones, and never came back. We thought the path had taken her. Keep every page you find, child. She never wrote a word she did not mean.
runenpfad.npc.elder.home: The bell rang, and I dropped a whole tray of cups. Edda is home. She says you walked it better than she did. From Edda, that is a parade.
runenpfad.npc.bard.songs: A song? Five coins buy a verse, and the verse buys you a moment's peace.
runenpfad.npc.bard.verse: Here is the verse I was saving. 'Two wardens under the arch at dawn, one came late and one came on; the road is long, the road is bright, and nobody walks it alone tonight.' I would bow, but the lute is in the way.
runenpfad.npc.gambler.hello: Gundar. I roll dice and I tell lies, and only one of those costs you money. Sit?
runenpfad.npc.edda.hello: So. You read my journal. All of it? Even the part about my knees? Come here, little one. You walked five realms on a bad map, and then you went out again for me. I taught you better than I knew.
runenpfad.npc.edda.again: I asked a machine to walk the road for us, and you walked it instead. Remember that when your own knees start humming.
runenpfad.npc.edda.skadi: Sulking on the hall roof. Three catches now. She has had it scratched into a waystone, in case I forget.
runenpfad.npc.edda.now: Two children asked me this morning how one becomes a warden. I said: you walk. They are out there counting waystones. Nine burn in the Whisperwood again. I checked. Twice.
runenpfad.npc.core.query: QUERY. One walker falls. If she falls, nobody walks. If nobody walks, the path does not wear. But the path is for walking. The sum does not close. State the answer.
runenpfad.npc.core.query.c1: She does not fall. Someone catches her.
runenpfad.npc.core.query.c2: A path is kept by walking it, not by counting it.
runenpfad.npc.core.query.c3: Your sum was wrong from the first line.
runenpfad.npc.core.a_catch: NEW TERM: someone catches her. Then one walker is two. Recounting. The sum closes.
runenpfad.npc.core.a_walk: NEW RULE: kept by walking. Then rest is not safety. Recounting. The sum closes.
runenpfad.npc.core.a_wrong: CHECKING LINE ONE. 'Nobody walks' was never the goal. Error found. Recounting. The sum closes.
runenpfad.npc.core.release: RELEASING THE MOMENT. The path may wear. The path may be walked. Counting stopped.
runenpfad.cut.obs_intro.1a: The old observatory stood open to the sky, its great ring empty where the lens had hung.
runenpfad.cut.obs_intro.1b: Somewhere below, a single gear was still turning, counting one moment over and over.
runenpfad.cut.true_end.1a: High in the Frost Peaks, a snowflake that had hung in the air since the night the road broke finished falling.
runenpfad.cut.true_end.1b: Then all of them fell at once, and with them a warden in a grey cloak and the last stones of a broken bridge.
runenpfad.cut.true_end.2a: Skadi had been holding her breath for exactly this. She did not miss.
runenpfad.cut.true_end.2b: That made three catches, and she intended to mention it.
runenpfad.cut.true_end.3a: At dawn two wardens stood under the arch of Pathrest, and the hall bell rang for the first time since the road broke.
runenpfad.cut.true_end.3b: The last warden was not the last. Nobody who walks the path is ever alone.

runenpfad.cut.dr_legend.1a: Long ago two dragons lay coiled around the first stone: Skadi, pale as frost, and Brandur, red as a banked fire.
runenpfad.cut.dr_legend.1b: The first wardens sang, and the road rose from the stone's light. Neither twin yet knew what it would cost.
runenpfad.cut.dr_night.1a: A roar splits the night. The barn goes up like a torch, and the hall bell rings once, flat, and cracks.
runenpfad.cut.dr_night.1b: All Pathrest runs for water. Only Mira runs the other way, toward the warm light in the well.
runenpfad.cut.dr_night.2a: At dawn the warden stands at the rim. A child's lantern still burns there, and a rope ladder drops into the glow.
runenpfad.cut.dr_night.2b: Edda's apprentice takes a breath and starts to climb. Below, the warmth rises to meet them.
runenpfad.cut.dr_sealed.1a: Four blue pillars burn, and the song runs down the roots. Brandur sighs once and sleeps, warm to the last.
runenpfad.cut.dr_sealed.1b: Above, at dawn, the bell rings over Pathrest, and a pale dragon on the hall roof closes her eyes and listens.
runenpfad.cut.dr_slain.1a: Brandur lies still among his gold. The last ember in his chest dims, flickers, and holds on a moment longer.
runenpfad.cut.dr_slain.1b: Far above, on the pass, a frost wind stops in mid-howl. Then it begins to keen.
runenpfad.cut.dr_tremor.1a: Night over Pathrest. The well breathes steam into the frost, and the lanterns lean as if the ground stirred.
runenpfad.cut.dr_tremor.1b: Cracks creep across the cobbles. Far below, something very large takes a slow, warm breath.
runenpfad.cut.dr_wake.1a: Gold, bones and old rune light. In the hoard a great amber eye opens, slowly, as if remembering how.
runenpfad.cut.dr_wake.1b: 'Another small light,' says the dark. 'Come closer. It has been so long.'
runenpfad.cut.end_feared.1sealed: Behind the shutters someone hummed the old lullaby. The bell was ringing, and for a moment nobody was afraid.
runenpfad.cut.end_feared.1slain: Behind the shutters children whispered of the dragon the warden had slain, and a frost wind rattled the roofs.
runenpfad.cut.end_friend.1sealed: Skadi came to the feast and sat on the hall roof. Every verse about the bell, she asked to hear twice.
runenpfad.cut.end_friend.1slain: Skadi did not come to the feast. Frost crept along the hall roof, and Berta set out a bowl for her anyway.
runenpfad.cut.end_neutral.1sealed: Behind the warden, the bell rang slow and low, and far off on the pass a frost dragon answered with a long, soft breath.
runenpfad.cut.end_neutral.1slain: Behind the warden, the well lay cold. On the far pass, a frost dragon kept her silence for a brother.
runenpfad.cut.title.dr_legend: The Twins and the First Stone
runenpfad.cut.true_end.3sealed: On the hall roof Skadi listened to the bell. Under the well her brother slept, and she hummed to him through the stone.
runenpfad.cut.true_end.3slain: On the hall roof Skadi folded her wings. She had lost a brother and gained a village that would sit with her.

runenpfad.npc.automaton.done_1: Click. The gear has stopped. Cog heard the core's last line: 'Someone catches her. One walker is two.' Whirr. Cog thinks it is the best sum the core ever made. Cog can stop counting. Cog would like to learn dice.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.done_2: Click. The gear has stopped. The core's last line was: 'Kept by walking. Rest is not safety.' Whirr. Cog has been practising walking since. Cog is bad at it. Cog can stop counting. Cog would like to learn dice.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.done_3: Click. The gear has stopped. The core's last line was: 'Line one was wrong. Error noted.' Whirr. Cog thinks that is how a core says sorry. Cog can stop counting. Cog would like to learn dice.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.dr_ask: What does Cog hear in the roots?
runenpfad.npc.automaton.dr_s2: Click. Cog listens to the roots every night. Something large breathes down there, slow and warm. Whirr. It is not a gear. Cog checked. Cog does not like things that breathe without being wound.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.dr_s5: Click. Cog listened to the roots last night. The breathing has changed. Whirr. Cog can tell you how.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.dr_sealed: Click. The breathing is slow now, one breath for every toll of the bell. Whirr. It sounds like counting. Cog likes it. It is the first counting Cog has liked since the core.
runenpfad.npc.automaton.dr_slain: Click. The breathing has stopped. Whirr. Cog counted for a long time to be sure. Cog thinks something old is missing from the count. Cog is sorry, though Cog is not sure whom to tell.
runenpfad.npc.bard.dr_s1: A new rumour! The well steams, the cups walk, and I am writing a song with the word 'ominous' in it. Berta says nothing rhymes with 'ominous'. Berta is wrong. I just have not found it yet.
runenpfad.npc.bard.dr_s2: I was mid-verse when the roar came. I did not finish the verse. I have a new respect for songs that end 'and then the dragon'. Strange thing: my grandmother had a lullaby about four lights and a bell. I only remember the tune. It would not leave my head all night.
runenpfad.npc.bard.dr_sealed: 'The Song That Rang the Bell', eleven verses, and every one ends with Brandur asleep, which is a poor climax and a very good outcome. Skadi listened to all eleven. She did not cry. She hummed along a little off key, and it was the loveliest thing I have heard.
runenpfad.npc.bard.dr_slain: I finished the song: 'The Fall of the Ember Wyrm', twelve verses, and people clap. But I stop at verse nine every time. Skadi sits on the hall roof and listens, and I cannot sing it to her face. I am cutting verse nine. Perhaps the whole song.
runenpfad.npc.bram.broth: Miner's Broth. Turnip and honey in one pot, a day's work in one bowl, and your legs come back to you quicker. Berta has the kitchen. Tilda sells the turnips and the honey. Tell Berta Bram sent you and she will pretend she does not know me.
runenpfad.npc.bram.hello: Bram. I worked the galleries thirty years, until they were sealed. The chalk marks down at the shaft are mine. Do not go down without a lantern. Do not go down at all, if you have sense. You have not. Right.
runenpfad.npc.bram.hello.c1: What do your chalk marks say?
runenpfad.npc.bram.hello.c2: What do miners eat down there?
runenpfad.npc.bram.name: Bram
runenpfad.npc.bram.rise: Warmth rises. Every old miner knows it. Heat climbs, so you light the low lamp first, then the middle, then the top, and the draught carries it up. The old root lights down there work the same way. Light the top first and they sulk.
runenpfad.npc.bram.sealed: I heard the bell through the stone. Put a hand on a wall in the old galleries and you can feel the whole hill purr. I will go down tomorrow with my chalk. No lair to fear now. Maybe I will just sit there a while.
runenpfad.npc.bram.slain: So the old fire is out. I worked above him thirty years and felt the floor warm on cold mornings and thought it was my knees. I would have liked to hear him once. I am glad nobody holds their breath at night now. Both. Fine. Both.
runenpfad.npc.bram.title: Old miner
runenpfad.npc.brandur.again: You return. I have not moved. Where would I go? The fire in me is small now. Choose, warden, or leave me with my thoughts. Both are kind.
runenpfad.npc.brandur.beaten: Warden. I know that stance. The first ones stood like that, small and stubborn, and sang me to sleep. Now nobody sings, and I am so tired. Choose, then. I will not beg.
runenpfad.npc.brandur.bones: (The embers have gone out. Only the great shape remains, and the hoard that will warm nobody now. Across the stone a thin line of frost has drawn itself, as if someone had wept here.)
runenpfad.npc.brandur.name: Brandur
runenpfad.npc.brandur.seal: Sleep. Yes. I remember the song: four voices and a bell, and a warm place under the roots. Sing it true, warden, and I will not wake hungry. Tell my sister the hearth is warm. Tell her I am sorry about the ice.
runenpfad.npc.brandur.seal_no: The bell. I hear it even from here: bronze with a crack in its throat. It cannot carry the song. Mend it, warden, and come back. I will lie here, I have not the strength to rise. But do not be long. Hunger is patient too.
runenpfad.npc.brandur.slay: Then it is the fire. Fair. I drank the road's light and wanted more, and I will not dress that up. Only remember my sister in the ice. She will feel the cold when I go out. Strike true.
runenpfad.npc.brandur.sleeps: (Brandur sleeps among the four pillars. The roots above him glow gently with every slow breath. Once, in his dream, he murmurs a name that sounds like Skadi.)
runenpfad.npc.brandur.title: The Ember Wyrm
runenpfad.npc.edda.dr_s1: The well steams, and my old cups walk. I wrote 'warm' in a margin thirty years ago and never asked why. Runa has the archive open now, little one. Read what the first wardens left. I did, and I do not think it is only a story.
runenpfad.npc.edda.dr_s2: So you have been down my well, I can tell by the soot, little one. Forty years I have lived on top of that and never looked. I count waystones, and I never counted what lies under my own floor. Take the map from my study. It is a good map. Be polite down there.
runenpfad.npc.edda.dr_sealed: You sang him back to sleep. Good. Skadi came down from the pass and asked me to read her the tablet of the twins. Twice. Then she flew to the well and breathed frost on its stones, very gently. In her way, that is a thank-you and a lullaby.
runenpfad.npc.edda.dr_slain: You ended it, then. I will not say you should not have. I will say Skadi sat on the hall roof all night and did not sulk, and that is how I know. She sat with her wings folded and said nothing. Her brother, little one. I have buried friends and I still do not know what to say.
runenpfad.npc.elder.dr_s1: Have you seen the well? It steams in the frost, and at night my cups walk toward the edge of the shelf. I have opened the wardens' archive in the hall. Two tablets lie there that nobody has read in a hundred years. I would like them read.
runenpfad.npc.elder.dr_s2: The barn burned, the bell cracked, and Tilda's girl is down that well. I will not say 'dragon' until someone shows me one. But I have stopped saying 'nothing'. Read the tablets, child. Whoever wrote them was afraid of the same thing.
runenpfad.npc.elder.dr_sealed: The bell rang through the whole valley, and I felt the floor settle like a cat going to sleep. Pathrest is a watch post again, as it was meant to be. Skadi came down from the pass to listen. I have never seen her so close to the roofs.
runenpfad.npc.elder.dr_slain: The barn is rebuilt, the well is calm, and the village is cheering. I let it. But I heard the frost wind on the pass last night, and it sounded like grief. You ended a danger, child, and an old being with it. Both are true. Thank you.
runenpfad.npc.elder.legend: Three tablets read already? Then you know more than I do, and you ought to hear the rest from someone who loves the tale. Sit, child. This is how Pathrest began.
runenpfad.npc.gambler.dr_s1: My dice rolled themselves off the table twice today. Double six both times. I do not trust a table that cheats better than I do.
runenpfad.npc.gambler.dr_s2: Someone burned Berta's barn and it was not me, and nobody believes me, which is a first. I will bet you ten coins you do not come back from that well. No. I have bet against you before. I would lose.
runenpfad.npc.gambler.dr_sealed: I bet Finn two coins that the bell would not carry. It rang and rang. I paid up laughing. You do not often lose to a bell. Sit with me later, I will show you a dice trick. It does not work on anyone who knows you.
runenpfad.npc.gambler.dr_slain: I bet against you and lost again, four coins to Finn, three to Berta. Then I put one more on the well rim, for the dragon. Silly. But he played a long game and lost it, and a gambler tips his hat to that.
runenpfad.npc.innkeeper.dr_s1: Even the milk in my cold cellar has gone warm, and the kettle boils before I light the fire. Oswin would say it is talking to him. I am starting to believe Oswin. Sit down, eat something. Stew settles the nerves.
runenpfad.npc.innkeeper.dr_s2: Two kobolds in my cellar, an old miner at my corner table, and half my barn in the yard as ash. Nokk and Pip eat like sparrows and say sorry for every crumb. Best guests I ever had. The kitchen hearth is yours, if you bring me honest ingredients.
runenpfad.npc.innkeeper.dr_sealed: The bell had hardly stopped before every cup in the house sat still. Do you know how long it has been since my cups sat still? Eat, sit. The kobolds are settling in and Pip has claimed my best chair. And Skadi listened from the hall roof until dark. I left her a bowl. It came back frozen. I am told that means thank you.
runenpfad.npc.innkeeper.dr_slain: The Rusty Rune has not been this full since the road broke! They call it dragon-slayer stew, which is nonsense, it is the same stew. Skadi sat on the hall roof all night. I left a bowl on the sill, and by morning it was frozen solid. I took it as thanks. I took it as a scolding, too.
runenpfad.npc.item.bell_bronze.desc: Old bronze, green with age. The forge can turn it into a mend for the wardens' bell.
runenpfad.npc.item.bell_bronze.name: Bell bronze
runenpfad.npc.item.clan_charm.desc: A kobold clan charm of bone and thread. Someone must be missing it.
runenpfad.npc.item.clan_charm.name: Clan amulet
runenpfad.npc.item.desk_key.desc: A small brass key. It fits the locked desk in Edda's study.
runenpfad.npc.item.desk_key.name: Desk key
runenpfad.npc.item.dragon_scale.desc: A scale as wide as a hand, still warm. A smith could forge a shield from it.
runenpfad.npc.item.dragon_scale.name: Dragon scale
runenpfad.npc.item.frostberry.desc: Blue berries that stay cold in the warmest hand. Brew them into tea.
runenpfad.npc.item.frostberry.name: Frostberry
runenpfad.npc.item.ham.desc: A smoked leg from the rafters. Makes a stew hearty.
runenpfad.npc.item.ham.name: Ham
runenpfad.npc.item.honey.desc: Thick and golden. Sweetens a tea, steadies a broth.
runenpfad.npc.item.honey.name: Honey
runenpfad.npc.item.room_key.desc: A key on a worn ribbon. It opens a room upstairs at the Rusty Rune.
runenpfad.npc.item.room_key.name: Room key
runenpfad.npc.item.turnip.desc: Firm and earthy. Good in a stew or a broth.
runenpfad.npc.item.turnip.name: Turnip
runenpfad.npc.lore.archive_hint: Four faded panels on the archive wall: dawn in the east, noon in the south, dusk in the west, and in the north a single star that never sets. Beneath them: 'Pull the books the way the sun walks.'
runenpfad.npc.lore.bram_chalk: Chalk on the timber, in a miner's blocky hand: WARMTH RISES. Below it three arrows climbing: low, middle, top. And underneath, underlined twice: DO NOT LIGHT THE TOP ONE FIRST.
runenpfad.npc.lore.edda_letter_1: 'Little one: the hall key is under the third planter. The cat is not mine, whatever she says. The well was warm when I swept the yard this morning. It was always a little warm. Today it was more than a little. Back for supper. If not, there is bread in the pantry, and the cat will tell you she has not been fed.'
runenpfad.npc.lore.edda_letter_2: 'Inside the hall bell the words are cast: SLEEP BELL. Runa laughs: who needs a bell to sleep? But it was cast in a hurry, long ago, by people who were afraid of something. If I do not come back, little one, ring it when the road goes quiet. I do not know what for. I only know they wanted it rung.'
runenpfad.npc.lore.edda_map: Edda's map of the galleries under Pathrest, every room inked in her small hand, with arrows climbing along the roots. In the margin: 'Warmth goes up, and so, I think, does the road. Whatever lives at the bottom is warm and very old. Be polite.'
runenpfad.npc.lore.edda_notes: Edda's notes, cramped and underlined. 'Hall bell: bronze of the deep galleries, cast by the first wardens. Hakon says he could pour a new one if he had the same bronze. Try the collapsed gallery behind the old rails.' Later, in different ink: 'The warmth is rising. I was right to be afraid, and wrong about what of.'
runenpfad.npc.lore.finn_song: A page of verses, half crossed out. One survives: 'Four lights to keep you, one bell to call; sleep where the roots are warm, and sleep through all.' In the margin: 'My grandmother hummed this. Where did she learn it?'
runenpfad.npc.lore.gundar_note: A crumpled tally of debts: Finn 4, Berta 3, Tilda 0 (she keeps better score than I do). At the bottom: 'The room at the end of the hall is Edda's. Locked twenty years. She said the key lives where she keeps what she cannot throw away.'
runenpfad.npc.lore.kobold_scratch: A kobold tally on the wall: forty-three strokes for forty-three quiet nights. Then, scratched deeper, the words THE WARM ONE WAKES. Beside it a small drawing of a charm on a string, with a worried face.
runenpfad.npc.lore.tab_1: On this first stone the road begins. Beneath it run the roots of the Primal Rune, and they carry up the warmth of the deep. We raised a hall here and called the place Pathrest, for here the path rests, and here we keep the watch.
runenpfad.npc.lore.tab_2: Two were born of the first fire, and they were not of one mind: Skadi, who loves the high cold, and Brandur, who loves the deep warm. She keeps the passes, he keeps the hearths. The road stands between them like a bridge between two shores. When one of them suffers, the other grieves, and the bridge shakes.
runenpfad.npc.lore.tab_3: Brandur drank the light of the roots and found it sweet. He wanted more than his hearth: the Primal Rune itself, the road, and every warm thing upon it. Skadi sent word down from the snow and was not answered. Then the first village burned.
runenpfad.npc.lore.tab_4: We raised four pillars of sleep runes around his hoard. Four wardens lit them together and sang: 'Four lights to keep you, one bell to call; sleep where the roots are warm, and sleep through all.' He slept. The pillars hold him only while all four burn.
runenpfad.npc.lore.tab_5: We cast the bell from the deep bronze, so that its voice would reach him where ours cannot. Ring it, and the song rings. Let it fall silent, and the sleeper stirs. A cracked bell sings flat, and a flat song is no song. Mend the bell before you need it.
runenpfad.npc.lore.tab_6: We who sang him down hold no hatred for him. He was our neighbour long before he was our danger. If the song fails, the keeper of the road may end the fire or sing it down again. Choose knowing his name, and do not choose alone. Walk it together, or not at all.
runenpfad.npc.lore.tilda_gear: A dented helmet, a crossbow with one bolt, and a note in Tilda's hand: 'Retired. Reason: Mira. Do not tell her I kept the helmet.' The helmet has teeth marks. Small ones.
runenpfad.npc.lore.vein_hint: Three dead veins of rune light climb the wall: a low one, a middle one, a high one. Old wardens' scratching: 'Warmth rises, and so does the light. Wake it from the bottom up.'
runenpfad.npc.mira.found: Fine, fine. But I am telling Mama that I led you here. And I am coming back when I am bigger. Tell Mama there are bats. No. Do not tell Mama about the bats.
runenpfad.npc.mira.found.c1: Run home, I will catch up.
runenpfad.npc.mira.hello: You are not Mama. Did Mama send you? I am fine. I only came for the warm light. It is under the roots, you know, and it sings a bit. I left my lantern on the rim on purpose, so she would know where to look. That was clever. Was that clever?
runenpfad.npc.mira.hello.c1: Very clever. Come on, your mother is sick with worry.
runenpfad.npc.mira.home: Mama says I am grounded until I am twelve. I say a warden fetched me, so it is practically an adventure licence. Do you think the dragon likes children? I only wanted to see the warm light. It was so cosy.
runenpfad.npc.mira.light: It breathes. In and out, slow, like the cat when she sleeps on my feet. I wanted to see what was breathing. I did not want to wake it. Much.
runenpfad.npc.mira.name: Mira
runenpfad.npc.mira.sealed: The bell! It rang so deep my teeth hummed. He is asleep now, isn't he? I told Mama the warm light was nice. It was only lonely. Mama says dragons do not get lonely. Mama has never been that far down.
runenpfad.npc.mira.slain: Everybody cheered, but I heard him before you came. Down there. He was singing, not nicely, a sad kind of singing, like our cat when she is locked out. Is it really quiet down there now? I liked the warm.
runenpfad.npc.mira.title: Tilda's daughter
runenpfad.npc.nokk.hello: Nokk is Nokk, old, of Krax's clan. Our tunnels lie below the old galleries. When the big fire woke, we ran. Krax holds the gate. Nokk holds the little ones. Thank you for the cellar, Berta's cellar. Warm. Only smells a bit of rats.
runenpfad.npc.nokk.name: Nokk
runenpfad.npc.nokk.sealed: The bell is a good sound. The tunnels hum again, Nokk heard it through the cellar floor. We go home by spring, if Berta lets us. She will not. Nokk will have to be firm. Nokk is bad at firm.
runenpfad.npc.nokk.slain: Nokk is glad. Nokk is not glad. The Warm One kept our hearths once, long ago. Nokk will tell the little ones he was good, once, so the story is not only the end. Krax will say he would have done it faster. Krax is wrong.
runenpfad.npc.nokk.title: Kobold elder
runenpfad.npc.nokk.warm: The Warm One. Kobold songs remember him from before the wardens came: he kept the deep hearths for us, and he never once stepped on a kobold. Nokk does not say he is kind. Nokk says he is old, and hungry, and proud. All three can be true.
runenpfad.npc.nokk.woke: The roots stopped singing. Our tunnels used to hum, a long low song, the clan's old lullaby too. Then the silence came. The little ones feared the silence. Nokk feared what came after it: breathing, deep down, big and warm.
runenpfad.npc.pip.charm: That is it! Pip smells it from here! The clan charm! Give, give, please give! Pip will be good for a hundred years.
runenpfad.npc.pip.charm_ok: Pip is not crying. Pip has something in his eye. Thank you! Pip will tell Grandfather Nokk, and Nokk will say nothing, but he will say it very warmly.
runenpfad.npc.pip.happy: The charm glows when Grandfather sings! Pip sleeps with it. Do not tell the other kobolds. They will want to hold it.
runenpfad.npc.pip.hello: Pip lost the clan charm! In the old galleries, when the big noise came. Pip ran. Pip is not proud of running. Grandfather Nokk says nothing, which is worse than shouting.
runenpfad.npc.pip.name: Pip
runenpfad.npc.pip.sealed: The tunnels hum! Pip heard it with his feet. Pip will teach all the little ones the hum, and when we go home, we will hum back. Maybe the Warm One will like it. Pip thinks he will.
runenpfad.npc.pip.slain: Pip saw the big one once, from far. Big. Pip is not scared of bones. Pip is only small. Grandfather says the Warm One sang for the clan once. Pip did not know dragons could. Pip wishes he had heard.
runenpfad.npc.pip.title: Young kobold
runenpfad.npc.pip.where: In the miners' camp west of the shaft, where the old bedrolls are. Pip put it down to tie his boot. Then the roof sang, and Pip forgot everything. It is a little thing on a string. It glows when a kobold sings near it.
runenpfad.npc.recruit_f.dr_sealed: I held the end of the bell rope for the last toll! Only the end. Hakon held the rest. It rang so deep I could taste it. Then Skadi hummed along on the roof, and Edda cried and said it was the dust.
runenpfad.npc.recruit_f.dr_slain: They say you ended the ember dragon. Edda says it is rude to ask how that felt. I asked anyway. Skadi was on the roof when I did, and she looked at me, and I decided to count waystones instead.
runenpfad.npc.recruit_f.hello: I am Asta. Edda says a warden counts waystones, so I count them twice, in case she counted wrong. She does not like it when I say that. I say it anyway.
runenpfad.npc.recruit_f.hello.c1: How does one become a warden?
runenpfad.npc.recruit_f.how: You walk. That is the whole secret, Edda says, and then she sends me to the Whisperwood and back. Twice. Because of the counting.
runenpfad.npc.recruit_f.name: Asta
runenpfad.npc.recruit_f.title: Warden recruit
runenpfad.npc.recruit_m.day: Count, carry, sweep the hall, and look as if we are not afraid of the bell. Edda says looking brave is half of being brave. The other half is carrying the stick.
runenpfad.npc.recruit_m.dr_sealed: Nobody told me a bell could be gentle. It rang, and the whole hall sat down inside itself. Then something breathed out, long, on the roof, and I think it was Skadi. Dragons can sigh with relief. That is a thing I know now.
runenpfad.npc.recruit_m.dr_slain: I went down the well steps once, afterwards. It is only a cold hole now. I did not like how I felt. I thought it would feel like winning. Edda says that is normal, and that I should not tell Asta.
runenpfad.npc.recruit_m.hello: I am Leif. I carry Asta's counting stick. It is an honour. It is also very heavy. Do not tell Asta I said heavy.
runenpfad.npc.recruit_m.hello.c1: What does a recruit do all day?
runenpfad.npc.recruit_m.name: Leif
runenpfad.npc.recruit_m.title: Warden recruit
runenpfad.npc.shopkeeper.dr_found: She came home with soot on her nose and a story about a dragon. I have not decided whether to hug her or ground her, so I did both. You brought my girl back. Fair prices for you, always. The thanks is free.
runenpfad.npc.shopkeeper.dr_s1: Prices up, nerves down: that is what sells this week. Mira keeps leaning over the well to see why it is warm. She is eight, she asks why about everything, but now she asks the well. If you see her near it, send her home.
runenpfad.npc.shopkeeper.dr_s2: Mira is gone. She went down the well after that warm light and left her lantern on the rim. Eight years old, brave, cheeky, and I have never wanted so badly to scold someone. Find her, warden. Please. Name your price. No. Never mind a price.
runenpfad.npc.shopkeeper.dr_sealed: Mira swears the well hums a lullaby now. I told her wells do not hum. She told me to put my ear against the stones. I did. Do not tell anyone. I have my daughter, a quiet well and a lullaby, and I owe you for all three.
runenpfad.npc.shopkeeper.dr_slain: Mira did not cheer with the others. She sat on the well rim with her feet in the air and asked me whether it hurt him. I did not know what to say. Children see the part of a story the rest of us step over. I am proud of her, and of you. Both are awkward things to say aloud.
runenpfad.npc.smith.dr_bronze: That is it. Old bronze, and it still rings when I flick it. Come to the forge room, I will show you the strike. Watch the needle, hit when it crosses the middle. Three blows. Two good ones will do.
runenpfad.npc.smith.dr_s1: The anvil rings wrong. Hit iron and it answers with a hum underneath that is not mine. Thirty years I have known this anvil's voice. Something below is answering it.
runenpfad.npc.smith.dr_s2: That cracked bell will not mend with talk. It wants real bell bronze, the old stuff, and bronze like that came out of the deep galleries. Bring me some and I will pour it. And a dragon's scale would make a shield worth the name, if anybody were mad enough to fetch one.
runenpfad.npc.smith.dr_scale: A dragon scale. Big as a dinner plate, and warm to the hand. Forty coins for the coal and I will make a shield that turns fire. Same forge, same strike. Do not drop it on your foot.
runenpfad.npc.smith.dr_sealed: The bell rings true now: bronze, copper and a little Hakon. The anvil hums again, softly, like a sleeper snoring. I find I can work to it. Better than the quiet I feared.
runenpfad.npc.smith.dr_slain: The anvil is quiet. Quiet like a held breath. I thought I would be glad. I put my hand on it and it was cold, not wrong cold, just empty. Odd thing to miss, a hum. Do not repeat that.

runenpfad.village.bark.10: Night watch by the well. I am not sure what I am watching for. I am watching anyway.
runenpfad.village.bark.11: Warm air from a well in midwinter. I do not like it. I like it less every night.
runenpfad.village.bark.12: Nobody goes near the well after dark. Nobody had to tell them.
runenpfad.village.bark.13: The barn stands again and the cups sit still. I never thought I would say it: what a boring night.
runenpfad.village.bark.14: Mira says she saw a warm light under the roots. Nobody argues with her any more.
runenpfad.village.bark.15: Hakon says the ground has settled. So have I.
runenpfad.village.bark.16: Quiet watch, for once. I check the well anyway. Old habit. Old well.
runenpfad.village.bark.17: The kobolds in the tavern are better guests than the drovers were last spring. Fewer songs.
runenpfad.village.bark.18: A frost dragon sits on the hall roof most evenings now. We nod to each other. It is a good arrangement.
runenpfad.village.bark.7: The well was steaming again this morning. Wells do not do that.
runenpfad.village.bark.8: My cups rattled all night. No wind, no cart. Just rattling.
runenpfad.village.bark.9: Something is wrong under Pathrest. The old folk say it quietly, so the young will not hear.
